content.text:
I submitted **index 7 (Sb 0.106 / Y 0.894)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.00138 %, the highest of the three I measured, but still very low. Under 2.1 eV light nothing I tested performed well.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 28 | 0.666 | −0.00017 (zero within noise) |
| 14 | 0.236 | 0.00008 (zero within noise) |
| 7 | 0.106 | **0.00138** |

- **Why it's low overall:** every known Sb–Y oxide phase in the database has a band gap too wide to absorb much 2.1 eV light.
- **XRD:** I scanned indices 15, 23 and 28, and all three gave the same pattern, apparently one fluorite-type structure. That didn't help choose where to spend the merit measurements.
- **How I chose the last measurement:** the first two readings were both effectively zero. I spent the third where the Gaussian-process model suggested, on the Y-rich side, and that point came out about 16 times higher than index 14.

I used all 3 merit measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD scans. The rest of the Y-rich end (indices 0–13) is unmeasured, so a better composition there is possible, but no merit measurements were left to check it.
